projects.title: Krishi Cobot — Agricultural Robotics
projects.description: Differential-drive agricultural robot with ROS2 integration, LiDAR sensing, and vision-based fruit inspection.

blocks.content: Differential-drive eBot navigates the field while a stationary UR5 arm handles manipulation at a fixed station. An OpenCV pipeline classifies fruit quality — distinguishing bad from good using shape and colour features. ArUco markers on the fertiliser can and the robot guide UR5 pick-and-place targets. LiDAR-based 2D shape detection triggers contextual behaviour changes in navigation.

projects.title: Drone Flight Controller
projects.description: Custom flight controller — sensor fusion, attitude estimation, cascaded PID loops.

blocks.content: Built a custom flight controller running FreeRTOS on STM32H7. Sensor fusion: IMU (MPU6050) + barometer (BMP280) with complementary filter.
Attitude estimation using quaternion-based Mahony filter — 1kHz update rate. Cascaded PID: outer loop for position, inner loop for angular rate.
Custom MAVLink implementation for ground station communication over UART.

projects.title: Robotic Arm — 6-DOF
projects.description: A 6-DOF robotic arm with full inverse kinematics, trajectory planning, and a custom BLDC controller.

blocks.content: Built a 6-DOF robotic arm from scratch using ROS2 and custom BLDC motor controllers. Implemented full inverse kinematics pipeline using analytical and numerical methods.

blocks.caption: Joint assembly — each joint uses a custom planetary gearbox

blocks.content: Trajectory planning with MoveIt2 — smooth interpolation across joint space. Custom PCB for motor driver with CAN bus communication between joints.

blocks.content: End-effector: 3-finger gripper with force feedback via strain gauges.

projects.title: Line Follower Robot
projects.description: High-speed line follower using STM32, IR sensor array, and adaptive PID with speed profiling.

blocks.content: STM32F4 based line follower achieving speeds above 1.5 m/s on curved tracks. 8-channel IR sensor array with weighted centroid algorithm for line detection.

blocks.caption: Top view — compact PCB with integrated sensor array

blocks.content: Adaptive PID controller — gain scheduling based on speed and error magnitude. Custom motor driver with DRV8833, PWM-controlled DC motors with encoder feedback.
Competed in national robotics competitions — podium finish at TechFest IIT Bombay.

blogs.title: UART Deep Dive
blogs.description: Everything about UART — framing, baud rate errors, DMA, and debugging tips.

blocks.content: UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter) is the backbone of embedded comms. Start bit → 8 data bits → optional parity → stop bit. Simple. But the devil is in the details.

blocks.caption: UART frame structure captured on a logic analyzer

blocks.content: Baud rate mismatch above 2-3% causes framing errors — always verify with a logic analyzer. DMA-based UART: offload transfers to DMA, CPU stays free for real work.
Debugging tip: if you see 0xFF or 0x00 garbage, check your baud rate and voltage levels. Overrun errors? Your ISR is too slow. Move to DMA or increase buffer size.

blogs.title: FreeRTOS from Scratch
blogs.description: A practical intro to real-time operating systems — tasks, queues, semaphores, priorities.

blocks.content: An RTOS gives you deterministic task scheduling — critical when timing matters. Tasks are independent threads with their own stack. Priority decides who runs when.
FreeRTOS scheduler: preemptive by default — higher priority task always wins. Queues: safe way to pass data between tasks. ISR-safe variants available.

Deadlock: Task A holds mutex 1 waiting for mutex 2. Task B holds mutex 2 waiting for mutex 1. Freeze. Priority inversion: low-priority task holds resource needed by high-priority task. Use priority inheritance.
Stack overflow is silent and deadly — enable stack watermark checking in debug builds.

blogs.title: PID Tuning in Practice
blogs.description: Tuning PID controllers for real hardware — Ziegler-Nichols, manual tuning, anti-windup.

blocks.content: PID = Proportional + Integral + Derivative. Three knobs, infinite headaches. P: reacts to current error. Too high → oscillation. Too low → slow response.

blocks.caption: Step response comparison — under, over, and critically damped

blocks.content: I: eliminates steady-state error. Too high → integral windup, overshoot, instability. D: reacts to rate of change. Dampens oscillation. Amplifies sensor noise.
Ziegler-Nichols: set I=0, D=0, increase P until sustained oscillation → use that as Ku, Tu. Anti-windup: clamp integrator when output saturates. Simple but essential.
Real hardware tip: always filter your derivative term. Raw derivative on noisy sensor = disaster.
